title: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA): First-Year Duties After 1 January 2026
hook: TRAIGA has been in force since 1 January 2026 — September 2026 is the first back-to-school and procurement cycle where Texas public bodies and covered deployers must show disclosure and prohibited-use controls
answer_first: The Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA / HB 149) took effect on 1 January 2026. It is a state-level governance statute, not a federal rule. It restricts certain government uses of AI (including social-scoring style systems and undisclosed biometric identification in specified public contexts), creates a Texas Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council, and requires disclosure when AI is used in covered interactions with individuals. Private-sector coverage is narrower than the EU AI Act: the operational burden falls first on Texas public bodies, contractors selling into those bodies, and deployers of the prohibited-use classes. As of 16 September 2026 — nine months after commencement — procurement teams should ask vendors for a TRAIGA mapping: which prohibited-use classes are designed out, where user disclosure fires, and what audit trail exists. Council of AI treats that mapping as a verified measurement credential. Language lock: monitored containment, not provable isolation. This page does not claim Texas certification, and it does not quote unpublished enforcement counts.
council_positioning: Monitored containment, not provable isolation. Verified measurement credential. UK-sovereign, AUKUS-compatible.
